title: A stop-loss order is not your maximum downside
summary: A stop-loss works in calm markets. In a crash you can be filled anywhere. The speaker says to plan with the worst case: an option position can lose 100% of its premium and a stock can go to zero. Ask whether the portfolio can absorb that loss, and avoid concentration in one name.

steps.caption: Equity positions: in the worst case one name can go bankrupt and go to zero.
Option overlay: the worst case is losing 100% of the premium paid.
Cash is the buffer that absorbs a loss.
Maximum downside is the full loss. A stop order does not limit it when prices gap.
Size each name so its worst case does not take you out: risk first, invest second, option overlays third.

takeaways: Stop-loss orders can fill far from the stop in a fast market.
Plan for the full loss: 100% of option premium, or a stock going to zero.
Limit concentration so one worst case is survivable.
